title: Noise exemption and BIA budgets approved
subtitle: Downtown and Belmont BIA budgets, tax rate by-law, and a 50th anniversary tribute to Waterloo Regional Police.
overview: A short special meeting dealt with two routine approvals. Council granted a noise exemption for the Grand River Hospital Foundation Rally for Health, held in the Sun Life parking lot at 969 King St W on May 27, with a second exemption for sound checks and rehearsals the evening before {{vote:m1}}. Neighbours near the site can expect amplified sound during those windows.

Council also approved the 2023 budgets for the Downtown Kitchener and Belmont Business Improvement Areas {{vote:m2}}. These budgets are referenced in the 2023 Tax Rate By-law, which council gave three readings later in the meeting, setting the City's 2023 tax rates and the payment of taxes after interim billing.

Council then went in camera to consider a land acquisition matter and a labour relations matter {{vote:m3}}. The minutes report no public outcome from that session. The Mayor also presented a plaque to the Chief of the Waterloo Regional Police Service marking the service's 50th anniversary during Police Week 2023. There was no recorded debate on any of the decisions.

decisions.detail: Council exempted the Grand River Hospital Foundation Rally for Health at 969 King St W from the noise by-law on May 27 from 4pm to 10pm, plus sound checks on May 26 from 5pm to 8pm.
Council approved the 2023 budgets of the Downtown Kitchener and Belmont Business Improvement Areas under the Municipal Act, 2001.

debate: No delegations registered, and the transcript records no discussion on the noise exemption or the BIA budgets; both went straight to a vote.
The noise exemption had already been considered earlier that day by the Community and Infrastructure Services Committee, and was brought forward from there.
In the police anniversary presentation, the Mayor praised the service's partnership with the City, including emergency response, work with the downtown BIA and the youth mentoring program.
The Police Chief said future public safety depends on partnerships on issues such as mental health, addictions, housing and homelessness.
